subject: [PATCH 3/4] memcg: manipulate memcg private ID references by ID

reviews.author: Bingfang Guo
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that mem_cgroup_private_id_put() requires rcu lock, but its purpose as a universal put function is not immediately obvious to users, and suggested adding a kdoc comment for clarity.
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks for pointing out this.

Agreed.  Both two callers are already holding the rcu lock so
taking the lock here is unnecessary. So I will drop the
rcu_read_lock() and use that in the next version!

My concern is that: mem_cgroup_private_id_put() looks like a
universal put function, requiring rcu held (which is true today)
is not that obvious to the users.  So I think adding a short kdoc
comment to make it clear later might be a good idea.

2026-09-19.patch_summary: This patch replaces the unnecessary locking mechanism in a specific function, allowing it to use the existing RCU (Read-Copy Update) read lock instead of acquiring an additional lock. This simplification ensures that the code adheres to Linux's lockdep rules and improves its overall efficiency.
